items.title: Dave Rivello interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rochester, New York, January 11, 2012
items.q: Jeff Campbell once said that playing bass in my band was like playing fourth trombone.

ctx.x: I was watching a YouTube selection, “Beyond the Fall.” I wondered if there’s parts in the piece that don’t necessarily have chord symbols that can be assigned to these four measures or whatever. Are you beyond thinking that way?

Sometimes. In that piece probably there’s moments where the soprano saxophone solo is and those backgrounds are happening and they get more and more dissonant, that it’s just, I think I just labeled it as like whatever area I was in harmonically, like D5. So it was just fifths in the bottom and then I let them try to navigate what all the stuff that’s happening around them once the backgrounds start coming in. Other than that there’s just a lot of sus chords I guess, that could be labelable but in general with my…
Wow. I like the idea of using the piano to double parts too. It definitely gives you a different tone. Not that many people employ it that way.
